title: A Protocol to Engineer Bacteriophages for Live-Cell Imaging of Bacterial Prophage Induction Inside Mammalian Cells
protocol: Pick single colonies of S. cerevisiae BY4741 and inoculate in 3 mL YPD broth a day prior to yeast recombination protocol.
Grow the culture at 30°C for 16 h.
Dilute the overnight grown cultures 1:10 into 30 mL of YPD broth and incubate at 30°C for 4 h.
Centrifuge cells at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 24°C.
Wash with 25 mL water and centrifuge as previously described.
Wash with 1 mL of 100 mM lithium acetate (LiAc) and centrifuge as previously described.
Perform the final resuspension in 240 μL of 100 mM LiAc.
Mix all PCR products (phage genome fragments and YAC) up to a total volume of 50 μL in an eppendorf tube.
Add approximately 1 μg of DNA per fragment and 300 ng of YAC.
Note: Concentrate the DNA during the PCR purification step to reach ∼1,000 ng/μL so that only 1 μL of each fragment is added.
Add approximately 1 μg of pRS415 plasmid DNA to 50 μL of water as a positive control.
Add 300 ng of the YAC vector to 50 μL of water as a negative transformation control.
Boil 2 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA at 95°C for 5 min.
Make three transformation mixtures, each with 50 μL yeast competent cells, 240 μL 50% PEG3350, 36 μL 1 M LiAc and 25 μL boiled salmon sperm DNA.
Combine each of the DNA mixtures (reaction mixture, negative and positive controls) with a transformation mixture.
Vortex the mixture gently at medium speed.
Incubate at 30°C for 30 min in a rotating nutator.
Incubate the mixture at 42°C for 45 min.
Centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 30 s.
Resuspend in 200 μL water.
Plate the transformants on SD-LEU plates and incubate at 30°C for 3–5 days.
Screen transformants for proper assembly after colonies become visible.
Expect a lawn of colonies when positive control prs415 is transformed.
Pick 8 colonies and resuspend each in 30 μL of H2O.
Mix 20 μL of colony suspension with 100 μL of freshly made 20 mM NaOH.
Incubate the mixture at 95°C for 10 min.
Vortex and centrifuge the sample at 8,000 × g for 1 min.
Use 1 μL of lysate as a template in a colony PCR reaction with each of the junction check primers using GoTaq Green Mastermix (Promega).
Inoculate 10 μL of suspension in 20 mL of SD-LEU liquid medium.
Grow cultures at 30°C for 3–5 days (or until OD600=1.0 is reached).
Stock yeast cultures containing YAC- λ constructs in 15% glycerol and store at −80°C.
Extract total yeast genomic DNA from a volume of cells containing OD600=10 equivalent using the YeaStarTM Genomic DNA Kit (Zymo Research) protocol I.
Perform PCR reactions for all junctions once more with the junction primer sets to confirm unwanted recombination did not occur during growth.
Store yeast genomic DNA for several weeks at 4°C prior to bacterial electroporation.
Mix 2.5 μL validated yeast gDNA with 25 μL of E. coli MegaX DH10B T1R Electrocomp Cells on ice.
Add 25 μL of transformation mixture in a 1-mm gap electroporation cuvette.
Electroporate at 2,000 V, 25 μF, and 200 Ω.
Chill cuvette, eppendorf tubes, and pipette tips on ice prior to electroporation.
Mix cells with 1 mL of Recovery Medium and recover at 37°C for 3 h.
Plate onto LB agar plates supplemented with 20 μg/mL kanamycin, and incubate for 16 h at 37°C.
Pick several colonies per lysogen, resuspend in 20 μL H2O.
Use 1 μL as template in a colony PCR reaction with primers across the attR site.
Generate plating cells for MG1655/pUC19 E. coli by growing them in LB supplemented with carbenicillin at 37°C for 16 hours.
Dilute E. coli plating cells 100-fold into 20 mL TB + 0.2% maltose and culture at 37°C until OD600=0.4 (approximately 2 hours).
Incubate cells on ice for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge cells at 3,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend cells in cold TB + 10 mM MgSO4 to a final OD600=2.0.
Grow lysogens from step 26 for 16 hours in 3 mL LB + kanamycin.
Dilute the lysogens 1:100 in LB + 10 mM MgSO4 + 0.2% glucose and grow at 37°C until mid-exponential phase.
Perform a 15-minute heat shock at 42°C prior to step 33 if working with a temperature-sensitive mutant of cI such as cI857.
Add glucose to the growth medium to repress expression of the phage receptor, LamB.
Mix 100 μL of plating cells with 100 μL of lysogen culture.
Add 3 mL of TB soft (0.7%) agar to the mixture.
Plate the mixture onto TB Carb plates.
Incubate the plates for 16 hours at 37°C.
Pick several cloudy plaques and store them in 100 μL of SM+gelatin buffer at 4°C.
Skim the top agar carefully when picking plaques.
Validate the phage for the presence of mKate by PCR.
Propagate the plaque to increase phage titer by performing a plate lysis protocol.
Grow a propagation host (MG1655/pUC19) overnight in LB for 16 hours.
Prepare propagation plates for phage.
Mix 1.2% Bacto Agar, 0.3% glucose, 2 mM MgSO4, 0.075 mM CaCl2, 0.004 mM FeCl3, and 0.01 mg/L Thiamine Hydrochloride in distilled water.
Autoclave the mixture.
Pour plates and let solidify while performing steps 38–39.
Dilute the bacterial propagation host culture 100-fold into 20 mL TB after 16 hours of growth.
Culture until OD600=0.4 at 37°C.
Mix resuspended plaques with 1 mL of propagation host, vortex at medium speed for 10 seconds and incubate at 4°C for a minimum of 15 minutes (up to a couple of hours).
Mix 350 μL of the mixture with 3 mL of soft TB agar and plate onto propagation plates.
Incubate the plates at 37°C without inversion until plaques cover the whole plate, typically less than 5 hours.
Add 5 mL of SM buffer to each plate and incubate for 2 hours on a shaking platform.
Re-collect 5 mL of buffer from the plate and add back 1 mL of fresh SM to the plate for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Combine the second SM harvest with the first, mix with 100 μL of chloroform and incubate at 24°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge lysates at 4,000 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Collect the top layer above the chloroform in a conical tube and wrap it in aluminum foil.
Store the collected phage particles in the dark at 4°C.
Mix 50 μL of plating cells with 50 μL of phage stock in serial dilutions from 1:103 to 1:109.
Incubate the plating cell/phage mixture at 37°C for 20 min.
Mix 100 μL of phage/cells mixture with 3 mL of soft agar (TB + 0.7% agar).
Plate the mixture onto TB Agar Carb plates.
Incubate the plated mixture overnight for 16 h at 37°C.
Count the number of plaques on the plate containing between 10 and 100 plaques.
Multiply the plaque count by the dilution factor and divide by the plating volume to get the titer in PFU/mL.
Dilute E. coli strains into fresh TB supplemented with 0.2% maltose and grow until early stationary phase (approximately 5 hours).
Centrifuge cells at 8,000 × g for 1 minute at 24°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of 10 mM MgSO4.
Incubate the resuspended cells for 1 hour at 30°C.
Mix 50 μL of cells with 50 μL phage at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 0.01 and incubate at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Combine the cell-phage mixture with 900 μL of pre-warmed LB + 10 mM MgSO4 and incubate for 45 minutes at 30°C.
Plate 100 μL of this mixture onto LB + kanamycin plates to select for kanamycin resistant phage lysogens.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 16 hours.
Grow validated lysogens for 16 h overnight at 37°C in LB with kanamycin and glycerol (15% glycerol).
Store grown lysogens at −80°C.
Inoculate single colonies of recombinant λ and WT-λ E. coli strains in 3 mL of LB at 37°C for 16 h.
Back-dilute the recombinant and WT lysogens in 3 mL of LB supplemented with 10 mM MgSO4 + 0.2% glucose and grow at 37°C until mid-exponential phase (OD600=0.4).
Serially dilute each bacterial culture in 1 mL of TB from 1:10 to 1:109.
Mix 50 μL of each dilution with 50 μL of plating cells.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 min to allow for phage DNA injection.
Add 100 μL of the phage mixture to 3 mL of 0.7% TB soft agar.
Plate the mixture onto TB Agar plates supplemented with carbenicillin.
Incubate plates overnight (16 h) at 37°C.
Count the number of plaques on the plate with between 10 and 100 plaques.
Calculate the spontaneous induction frequency (PFU/CFU) for the recombinant λ and WT-λ.
Validate that the phage reporter functions by performing live-cell imaging.
Inoculate and grow single colonies of non-lysogenic E. coli in 3 mL of LB at 37°C for 16 h.
Grow single colonies of lysogenic E. coli strain of recombinant λ in 3 mL of LB at 37°C for 16 h.
Dilute bacterial cultures 100-fold into two flasks each of fresh LB the next day.
Grow until mid-exponential phase (typically 2 h until OD600=0.4).
Add 50 ng/mL NFX to the lysogen and incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Keep the second culture unstimulated and continue to grow for 30 min.
Concentrate each bacterial strain to an OD600 of 0.2.
Spot 1 μL onto individual agarose pads.
Transfer agarose pads to a glass slide and pipette bacteria to the center of each pad.
Place the agarose pads, bacterial side down, on a Lab-tek chamber.
Seal the Lab-tek chamber with parafilm.
Wait 5 minutes for bacteria to dry onto the pads before imaging.
Seed RAW264.7-H2B-miRFP670 cells at a density of 1.5 x 10^4 cells/well on a fibronectin-coated 96-well glass imaging plate.
Incubate the cells in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 2 mM L-Glutamine.
Maintain the cells overnight to ensure they are less than 50% confluent by the day of infection.
Grow up single colonies of lysogenic and non-lysogenic strains overnight in LB supplemented with the appropriate antibiotic.
Pre-heat a large centrifuge with plate adapters to 34°C.
Back-dilute E. coli from those grown for 16 hours in LB cultures into fresh LB without antibiotics.
Grow diluted E. coli to mid-exponential phase (OD600=0.4).
Maintain RAW264.7 cells in antibiotic-free DMEM prior to infection.
If RAW264.7 cells were maintained with antibiotics, wash the cells twice with imaging media and add back 150 μL of IM.
For experiments using temperature-sensitive phage, grow lysogens at 30°C.
Wash bacteria twice with PBS.
Resuspend bacteria at the appropriate concentration to achieve MOI 10 for live-cell experiments.
Add 150,000 E. coli/well containing macrophages for MOI 10.
Centrifuge plates at 200g at 34°C for 15 min.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 1 h.
Wash cells two to three times with imaging media (IM).
Pipette from a consistent corner of the well during washing to avoid disturbing the cell monolayer.
Add back 150 μL of IM supplemented with gentamicin to each well after washing.
Seal the plate with an AeraSeal.
Immediately image the cells with the lid removed to ensure adequate gas exchange.
Use a Nikon Eclipse Ti fluorescence microscope encased in an environmental chamber maintained at 37°C and 5% CO2 for imaging.
Control the microscope using Micro-Manager software.
Acquire images on an Andor Neo 5.5 sCMOS camera.
For bacterial agar pad imaging, take at least two images per pad every 10 minutes with a 40×/0.95 numerical aperture objective + 1.5× tube lens and 2 × 2 binning for 3–5 hours at 37°C.
For infected mammalian cell imaging, capture images every hour with a 20×/0.75 numerical aperture objective and 2 × 2 binning for at least 18 hours.
Image an uninfected control well to monitor cell health throughout the time course.
Imaging includes at least three wells per strain and nine fields-of-view per well.
